October 19–22, 2026

Secretary Sonderling in California

Less than three weeks after he was sworn in as the 31st U.S. Secretary of Labor, Keith Sonderling spent four days traveling California from San Francisco to San Diego. Local workforce boards took part at several stops, bringing employers, colleges and training providers to meet him and showing how federal workforce dollars are put to work in their regions.

Photos: Secretary Sonderling on X and the Workforce Investment Board of Tulare County.

Monday19October

Day 1

From cybersecurity in San Francisco to agricultural technology in Merced

San Francisco→Modesto→Merced County

The week opened at a San Francisco software company and moved into the Central Valley by midday. From there, Prospero, Merced County’s workforce agency, led a North Valley program that took the Secretary from a Modesto training floor to an industry roundtable and a federally funded construction site, with workforce leaders from Merced, Stanislaus and San Joaquin counties along for the day.

Employer · Veterans

Elastic

San Francisco

Elastic’s participation in the Department of War’s SkillBridge program helps service members who specialize in cybersecurity move into civilian careers. The Secretary connected that work to the need for a cyber workforce that can prevent fraud and protect taxpayer dollars.

Sonderling on X

Workforce board partner · Training provider

VOLT Institute

Modesto · with Rep. Tom McClintock
Stanislaus County Workforce Development is one of the partners VOLT credits with making its model work, alongside regional manufacturers. Its director, Doris Foster, joined the Secretary for the North Valley program.

VOLT was the first stop of the North Valley program. The Secretary and Rep. McClintock toured VOLT’s accelerated, competency-based training in industrial automation, controls, robotics, electrical systems and maintenance, and met students. VOLT also tagged FANUC America, Amatrol, APT Manufacturing Solutions and Rockwell Automation as industry partners.

VOLT Institute on LinkedIn · North Valley THRIVE

Workforce board host · Roundtable

West-Mark and the Hunter Farms roundtable

Merced County
Prospero, Merced County’s workforce agency, organized the North Valley program. North Valley THRIVE, the tri-county regional coalition housed at Prospero, noted that leaders from Merced, Stanislaus and San Joaquin counties took part.

After the Atwater High School Band welcomed him, the Secretary toured West-Mark and then sat for an industry roundtable in front of the historic barn at Hunter Farms. California Labor Secretary Stewart Knox, Stanislaus State President Britt Rios-Ellis, Stanislaus County Workforce Development Director Doris Foster and San Joaquin County WorkNet Director Patricia Virgen joined the day, along with Merced County Supervisors Daron McDaniel and Lloyd Pareira and County Executive Officer Mark Hendrickson.

The Manufacturers Council of the Central Valley told him that automation is increasing manufacturers’ need for skilled workers, and asked for a renewed Manufacturing Extension Partnership center, noting that California is one of only two states without one.

MCCV · Merced County · Sonderling on X

DOL grantee · Community college

Merced College AgTEC Innovation Center

Merced

The day ended at the construction site of the AgTEC Innovation Center, which is scheduled to open in 2027 with high-tech labs for nut, fruit, vegetable and meat processing, a product development kitchen, training classrooms and a retail farm market. DOL’s nearly $2 million investment supports the college’s AgTEC Workforce Initiative, including a competency-based Ag Systems certificate for current farmworkers that won the college a 2026 Bellwether Award in Workforce Development.

College leaders also presented AgTEC Coast-to-Coast, a partnership with the University of Florida, the College of Central Florida, the City of Newberry and the F-300 AgFoodTech ecosystem. President Chris Vitelli credited the Merced County Workforce Development Board with coordinating the visit.

“The Innovation Center is going to open doors for our students that simply haven’t existed before.”Cody Jacobsen, Dean of Agriculture and Industrial Technology, Merced College

Merced College · Chris Vitelli · Sonderling on X · ABC30

Tuesday20October

Day 2

Dairy, produce and the skills automation now demands

Tulare→Visalia→Shafter→Arvin

Tuesday moved south through Tulare and Kern counties. The conversation stayed on agriculture and food processing, and on what workers need now that more of the work runs on automated equipment.

Workforce board host · Roundtable

Saputo, California Dairies and an employer roundtable

Tulare and Visalia
The Workforce Investment Board of Tulare County hosted the visit and convened WIB leadership, board members and employers from the Tulare-Kings Agriculture, Industrial and Healthcare industry partnerships.

The Secretary toured California Dairies, Inc. in Visalia, a cooperative co-owned by nearly 300 family dairy farms, and Saputo in Tulare, which hosted the roundtable after his plant tour. At the table, ten employer representatives from the industry partnerships described how industry change is reshaping the skills they need, where they struggle to find and develop talent, and how DOL could support businesses and strengthen workforce services. California Workforce Association Executive Director Adam Peck joined them to speak for the workforce development system.

“Our businesses help identify the skills and talent they need, and our workforce, education, and economic development partners listen and respond.”Jennie Bautista, Executive Director, Workforce Investment Board of Tulare County
“No one cares more about a community’s workforce and economy than the local business and community leaders who sit on workforce boards. When business, economic development, community colleges, K-12 schools and labor come together at that table, they work as one system that responds to the needs of industry and the families in their community.”Adam Peck, Executive Director, California Workforce Association, responding to the Secretary at the roundtable

Tulare WIB · Jennie Bautista · California Dairies · Sonderling on X

Apprenticeship · Employer training

Wonderful Career Center

Shafter

Wonderful’s training center runs a paid Maintenance Technician Apprenticeship that pairs on-the-job experience with college credit, along with a Powered Industrial Truck program. The Secretary later pointed to the company’s new logistics facility as a source of year-round jobs in a county where farm work keeps unemployment seasonal.

Sonderling on X · 23ABC

Employer · Roundtable

Grimmway Farms, Malaga facility

Arvin

An afternoon tour and roundtable at a company the Secretary called one of America’s leading producers of carrots, potatoes and organic vegetables, with a focus on the technology now used in processing. Afterward he sat down with 23ABC and described where he expects those new skills to come from.

Sonderling on X · 23ABC video

“Whether it’s automation, working with the automation, and that’s a new skill that workers are going to need, and they’re going to need it very specific to agriculture. So a big part of this too is not just working with employers in this field, but also talking to the workforce development boards, talking to community colleges, talking to the Pre-K-12 system of how we can get those skills that are changing in agriculture into schools.”
Secretary Sonderling to 23ABC News in Arvin, October 20
Wednesday21October

Day 3

A university and the jobs ahead of the 2028 Games

Arvin→Los Angeles

Over the Grapevine and into Los Angeles, the Secretary turned to university research and to the hiring that the 2028 Summer Olympics will bring to the region.

University · LA28

USC and the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum

Los Angeles

He met with university leaders and partners about USC’s research programs and facilities, then toured the Coliseum, a venue for the 2028 Games. He cited estimates that the Olympics will support more than 200,000 jobs across industries and over $8 billion in Games-related infrastructure projects.

Sonderling on X

Thursday22October

Day 4

Manufacturers that grow their own talent, and a university that trains working adults

Redlands→Temecula→La Jolla

The last day ran from the Inland Empire to the coast. Each stop showed an employer or university building its own pipeline, through student programs, on-the-job training and continuing education.

Employer · Youth pathways

Garner Holt

Redlands

Thursday began at Garner Holt Productions, an animatronics manufacturer that combines creative design with advanced manufacturing. Its education program, Garner Holt Education Through Imagination, gives students of all ages hands-on STEAM pathways into robotics, automation and skilled trades.

“We are incredibly excited about our shared vision for America’s future—one that emphasizes advanced manufacturing, immersive hands-on learning, workforce development, and innovative STEAM education for children and young adults across the country.”Germaine Garcia-Kaufman, Executive Vice President, Garner Holt Education Through Imagination

Sonderling on X · Garner Holt ETI

Workforce board involvement · On-the-job training

ScottsMiracle-Gro

Temecula
The Riverside County Workforce Development Board was part of the Temecula visit, represented by Stephanie Adams.

The Secretary toured the company’s Temecula plant, where it makes its fertilizer spreaders, and discussed how on-the-job training, high school employment programs and veterans initiatives help it build and keep its workforce. A company vice president noted that ScottsMiracle-Gro is continuing to invest in automation and new technology at the site.

Sonderling on X · Kurt Kroplin

Workforce training · University

UC San Diego Extended Studies

La Jolla

The trip closed at UC San Diego, where Extended Studies runs workforce training for employers in cybersecurity, biotech and healthcare. Extended Studies also hosted a business roundtable with the Secretary on strengthening workforce partnerships between employers and California’s colleges and universities.

Sonderling on X · Roundtable participant

“This week, as part of those efforts, I met with workforce and education leaders across California’s Central Valley to better understand their workforce needs and to see how innovative training programs are preparing the next generation for high-skilled, high-paying jobs.”
Secretary Sonderling on X, October 24, linking to the Workforce Investment Board of Tulare County’s story on the visit

Looking back on the week

What the Secretary took away

Local boards as conveners

Where boards were involved, they used the visit to put employers in front of the Secretary and let them describe their own hiring and skill needs, from the Tulare-Kings industry partnerships to the Merced roundtable and VOLT’s manufacturing partners.

In Arvin the Secretary named workforce development boards, along with community colleges and schools, as the partners DOL will work with to bring new technology skills to workers.

Federal investment on the ground

Merced College walked him through a building that DOL’s nearly $2 million grant is helping to fund. Wonderful’s paid apprenticeship and ScottsMiracle-Gro’s on-the-job training showed employers investing in their own workers.

Employers repeated one point throughout the week: automation is raising the skills they need to hire for.

Context

The policy backdrop

  • New in the role. The Senate confirmed Sonderling 47–41 on September 30, and he was sworn in on October 2. He had led the Department as Acting Secretary since April 2026 and served as Deputy Secretary from March 2025.
  • H-2A wage rule. ABC30 reported that a federal judge ruled in August that key parts of DOL’s revised method for calculating H-2A farmworker wages were unlawful and ordered replacement rules by December 30. The Secretary said the Department continues to defend the rule. United Farm Workers President Teresa Romero criticized the Department’s handling of the issue.
  • A national tour. The California trip was part of a run of employer, university and community college visits. On Friday the Secretary was at KU Innovation Park in Lawrence, Kansas.
